passages.text: Chief complaint: headache for three weeks, worse in the morning.
History: patient reports intermittent double vision beginning about ten days ago. No prior history of migraine. No recent head trauma.

Neurologic exam: alert and oriented. Cranial nerves II through XII assessed; mild limitation of left lateral gaze with horizontal diplopia on left gaze. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. Sensation intact. Gait normal.
Fundoscopic exam limited; unable to fully assess optic discs in clinic.
Assessment: headache with new diplopia (R51.9, H53.2). Neurologic red-flag present.
Plan: order MRI brain. Referral to neurology placed. Return precautions reviewed.
